## Claim

The core reconciler passes its transport around as an UNANNOTATED parameter. That is why the Backend
port can silently under-declare what the core requires — the defect class behind
[rebar:a357-b747-ece9-4cf5], where a DC writing reconcile pass crashed on a method
(`set_entity_property`) that the core calls from three sites and `TicketTransport` never declared.

This is not an adjacent tidiness issue. It is the ENABLING CONDITION.

## Proof — three-way mypy probe

    def current_shape(client, ...):                     # today's core
        client.set_entity_property(...)                 # -> NO ERROR

    def annotated_any(client: Any, ...):                # what the ratchet alone accepts
        client.set_entity_property(...)                 # -> NO ERROR

    def annotated_port(client: TicketTransport, ...):   # typed as the PORT
        client.set_entity_property(...)
        # -> error: "TicketTransport" has no attribute "set_entity_property"  [attr-defined]

Run with the repo's own mypy settings (`--check-untyped-defs`, which IS already enabled globally).

Had the params been typed as the port, `set_entity_property` would have failed `make typecheck` at
AUTHORING TIME, forcing it onto `TicketTransport`; the DC transport would then have failed Protocol
conformance at its assignment site. The crash could not have reached a live instance.

## The important subtlety — the EXISTING ratchet does not fix this

`pyproject.toml` documents a shrink-only mypy strictness ratchet (per-package
`disallow_untyped_defs`, enforced by `test_mypy_ratchet.py`), currently enabling
`rebar.graph.*` and `rebar.grounding.*`, with `_engine` in the exempt set awaiting promotion.

**Promoting `_engine` through that ratchet would NOT have prevented a357** — see the middle row
above: `client: Any` satisfies `disallow_untyped_defs` and remains completely blind. The requirement
is not 'annotate the params', it is 'annotate them AS THE PORT'. A promotion done the easy way
(spraying `Any`) would close the ratchet ticket while leaving this defect fully intact, which is the
outcome to guard against.

## Scale (measured)

15 functions in `rebar_reconciler` take a `client`/`transport` parameter with NO annotation;
10 already annotate one. Sample untyped: `dispatch_one.create_one`, `dispatch_one.update_one`,
`dispatch_apply_phases._update_one_apply_reporter`, `batch_dispatch.delete_one`,
`apply_inbound.inbound_repair_property`.

## Interaction with J9 [rebar:bda8-370d-23ad-4e36]

J9 plans a STRUCTURAL TEST asserting every transport member the core reaches for is declared on the
port. Typing the params is strictly stronger and cheaper to maintain: mypy then enforces BOTH
directions (the core cannot call an undeclared member; a concrete transport must satisfy the
Protocol) at every build, with no bespoke AST walker to keep correct — and note my own AST walker was
wrong twice in this epic. J9 should probably ADOPT this rather than hand-roll the checker; sequencing
is a judgement call for whoever schedules them.

## Also explains [rebar:dbf9-3fc8-625d-4730]

The same `Any` is why Serena/Pyright returns a FALSE EMPTY for
`find_referencing_symbols('set_entity_property')` — no resolvable receiver type, so no references.
Typing the params fixes the navigation blindness as a side effect.

## Approach

**Annotate as the PORT, then let mypy find the port's gaps.** Replace each unannotated
`client`/`transport` parameter in `rebar_reconciler` with `TicketTransport` (or the narrower
capability Protocol where a site needs one). Then run `make typecheck` and treat every
`[attr-defined]` it reports as a FINDING, not as noise: each one names a member the core calls
that the port does not declare — exactly the a357 class. Resolve each by DECLARING the member on
the port (the core genuinely requires it) rather than by widening the annotation back to `Any`,
which is the failure mode this ticket exists to prevent.

**Expect the error list to be the real work.** The annotation edit itself is mechanical; the
substance is whatever mypy then reports. Do not pre-guess that list — probe it first and record it
on the ticket before editing, so the change's size is known rather than discovered halfway.

**Do NOT promote `_engine` through the strictness ratchet in this story.** The ratchet enables
`disallow_untyped_defs`, which `client: Any` satisfies while remaining completely blind — the
middle row of this ticket's own three-way probe. Promotion and port-typing are separate changes and
conflating them is how the easy version (spray `Any`) ships and closes both.

**Relationship to J9, settled rather than left open:** [rebar:bda8-370d-23ad-4e36] already landed
`assert_transport_conforms()`, a RUNTIME conformance guard wired into both backend factories. This
story is its STATIC complement, not its replacement. Both stay: the runtime guard catches a
transport that is built wrong, mypy catches a core call site that reaches for an undeclared member
at authoring time. Removing either is out of scope.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/**` — annotate the `client`/`transport` parameters.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py` — declare any member mypy proves the core calls
  and the port omits.
- one new test pinning that `Any` does not satisfy the requirement (see Testing).
- a note in `pyproject.toml` / `docs/architecture.md` per the last AC.

**NOT in scope:** promoting `_engine` through the mypy strictness ratchet; removing or weakening
J9's runtime `assert_transport_conforms()`; any behaviour change whatsoever — this story must not
alter what any function DOES.

## Testing

* `make typecheck` is clean at the resulting strictness, and `make lint` passes.
* the full reconciler unit suite passes UNEDITED — this is a pure annotation change, so any test
  that needs editing means behaviour moved and the change has failed its own premise.
* **the `Any` guard, which is the load-bearing test.** A check that fails if a core
  `client`/`transport` parameter is annotated `Any` (or left bare) rather than as the port. Without
  it, the next contributor satisfies the ratchet with `Any` and silently restores the blindness —
  and that is not hypothetical, it is the documented middle row of this ticket's probe.
* a NEGATIVE mypy probe, run and recorded: a scratch call to an undeclared member through a
  port-typed parameter must produce `[attr-defined]`, proving the annotation actually enforces
  something rather than merely being present.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] every `client`/`transport` parameter in the core reconciler is annotated with the PORT type
      (`TicketTransport`, or a capability Protocol where the site needs one), NOT `Any`
- [ ] `TicketTransport` declares every member the core calls, so `make typecheck` passes only when
      the port is complete — with the port-completeness gap of a357 either fixed or explicitly
      declared
- [ ] a test asserts an `Any`-annotated transport param does NOT satisfy this requirement, so a
      future 'annotate it to pass the ratchet' change cannot silently reintroduce the blindness
- [ ] `mypy src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler` is clean at the resulting strictness
- [ ] the ratchet note in `pyproject.toml` / `docs/architecture.md` records that annotating as `Any`
      satisfies `disallow_untyped_defs` but defeats its purpose at port boundaries
